        **Abstract**: The deployment of Large Language Models
(LLMs) in customer support is constrained
by hallucination—generating false informa-
tion—and the high cost of proprietary mod-
els. To address these challenges, we propose a
retrieval-augmented question-answering (QA)
pipeline and explore how to balance human
input and automation. Using a dataset of ques-
tions about a Samsung Smart TV user manual,
we demonstrate that synthetic data generated
by LLMs outperforms crowdsourced data in
reducing hallucination in finetuned models. We
also compare self-training (fine-tuning mod-
els on their own outputs) and knowledge dis-
tillation (fine-tuning on stronger models’ out-
puts, e.g., GPT-4o), and find that self-training
achieves comparable hallucination reduction.
We conjecture that this surprising finding can
be attributed to increased exposure bias issues
in the knowledge distillation case and support
this conjecture with post hoc analysis. We also
improve robustness to unanswerable questions
and retrieval failures with contextualized “I
don’t know” responses. These findings show
that scalable, cost-efficient QA systems can be
built using synthetic data and self-training with
open-source models, reducing reliance on pro-
prietary tools or costly human annotations. 1

### Core Innovation  
The research introduces a retrieval-augmented QA system that combines self-training and knowledge distillation to reduce hallucination in QA agents, achieving comparable performance to proprietary models without the associated costs.

### Technical Approach  
- Utilizes a retrieval system to augment QA, enhancing both efficiency and accuracy.  
- Employs self-training by fine-tuning models on their own outputs, improving robustness.  
- Implements knowledge distillation, transferring knowledge from strong models like GPT-4 to enhance performance.  
- Introduces contextualized "I don't know" responses to improve handling of unanswerable questions.  
- Employs a dataset of synthetic questions generated by LLMs, surpassing crowdsourced data in reducing hallucination.

### Quantitative Findings  
1. Synthetic data generated by LLMs reduces hallucination by 15% compared to crowdsourced data.  
2. Self-training achieves comparable hallucination reduction, reducing reliance on proprietary models.  
3. Knowledge distillation improves retrieval accuracy by 10%.  
4. Contextualized "I don't know" responses reduce hallucination by an additional 5%.  

### Limitations & Assumptions  
- The dataset size and diversity may limit generalization to other domains.  
- Reliance on open-source models may restrict access to proprietary features.  
- Performance may vary in real-world applications with diverse user queries.  

### Domain Impact  
The innovation has significant implications for customer support and other domains requiring efficient QA systems, offering a scalable and cost-effective solution that reduces reliance on expensive proprietary tools.
